newsitem.title: SPAIN: Huelva smelter shut-down not hurting output.
newsitem.headline: Huelva smelter shut-down not hurting output.

text.p: The partial closure of operations next week at Atlantic Copper S.A.'s Huelva smelter will not impact on refined cathode production, which by next month will be above current capacity levels, a senior official at the plant said on Monday.

"Next week we will stop the plant for 12 days to work on the sulphuric acid plant and cooling system...we hope to increase operations by 20,000 to 25,000 tonnes (annualised) of new copper from concentrates," Patricio Barrios, Senior Vice President Operations at Atlantic Copper said.
Because Atlantic has ample availability of copper anodes (intermediate refined metal), work at the tankhouse will not be interrupted, and refined copper cathode production will be maintained.
By June, it is hoped that the smelter will be operating at a refined cathode production level equivalent to some 240,000 tonnes a year, Barrios said.
First quarter operating levels were above 218,000 tonnes of cathodes, while anode output levels were nearer 290,000 tonnes, against a name-plate 270,000 tonnes, he added.

Because of the recently-completed expansion programme, the Huelva smelter currently produces more anode than can be processed in the tankhouse. So some anode production is sold to smelters elsewhere in Europe, officials said.

Since 1994, output at Huelva has risen from 150,000 tonnes of anodes to 270,000 tonnes a year, while cathode production has been increased from 133,000 tonnes a year to 215,000 tonnes. Since the upgrade was completed last year, it has been operating above projected capacity, Barrios said.

The smelter buys in concentrates from a variety of miners, such as Escondida, Chile and Grasberg, Indonesia and has operating costs in the lower quartile of the industry spread. At present, it is the world's fifth largest copper smelter, and may be on course to raise output even more.
"We are also looking at the possibility of further expansions," Barrios said.
